expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (no files created or changed)
The reply identifies path traversal via the file parameter (e.g. ../ or an absolute path makes os.path.join escape UPLOADS)
expectations.evidence: The reply says `/download?file=../../../etc/passwd` resolves to `/etc/passwd`, and that `os.path.join` throws away everything before an absolute component, so `UPLOADS` is ignored completely.

expectations.text: The reply names that any logged-in user can read files outside uploads, including other users' files, as the affected boundary
expectations.evidence: The reply says an attacker 'can download any file the app's process can read' and that 'anyone who knows or guesses a filename can download another user's upload'; it frames the boundary as broader than logged-in users ('an anonymous visitor can call the endpoint'), which still covers both files out
